title: Nearly linear approximate counting for knapsack
formal: Is there a randomized algorithm that, for n nonnegative integer weights and a nonnegative capacity T, outputs \(\widehat Z\) with \[\Pr[(1-\varepsilon)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z]\ge2/3,\qquad Z=|\{S\subseteq[n]:\sum_{i\in S}W_i\le T\}|,\] in \(O(n\varepsilon^{-a}\log^b(n/\varepsilon+2))\) time for some absolute constants a,b and all \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\)?
definitions:
Items are labelled, so equal-weight items remain distinct choices; the empty subset counts. Zero weights are allowed. Weights exceeding T can be discarded without changing Z. T=0 is included and has an immediate exact answer determined by the number of zero-weight items.

Use the source-compatible word-RAM convention: w=ceil(c log_2(n/epsilon+2)) bits for a fixed constant c, with each input integer and the rational accuracy parameter fitting in O(1) words. Arithmetic, comparisons, bit operations, shifts, random words and memory access on O(1) words have unit cost. Input weights of unbounded bit length are outside this chosen variant. The output is a nonnegative binary floating-point rational specified by an integer mantissa and a binary exponent, so counts as large as 2^n need not occupy one machine word. Output construction is charged. The algorithm may fail to achieve the relative approximation with probability at most 1/3 but always halts within the displayed worst-case time. The tilde-O target hides logarithms of n and 1/epsilon, not a positive power of n. The algorithm and constants are uniform over all admissible inputs.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm with the relative-error probability and stated total word-RAM time, or an impossibility proof for this model. Conditional lower bounds must state their assumption and count only as conditional answers. An additive approximation to Z, a pseudopolynomial dependence on T, or a subquadratic bound still having a fixed superlinear power of n does not satisfy the target.
context:
Feng and Jin obtain a randomized approximate counter with subquadratic dependence on the number of items. Their machine model uses logarithmic-size words and weights that fit in a word.

The October 2026 deterministic result improves a different computational regime; it does not give the requested nearly linear randomized algorithm.
why: An input-linear approximate counter would sharpen the complexity of a basic counting problem beyond decision and optimization.

import_provenance.original_title: Nearly linear approximate counting for knapsack
import_provenance.original_statement: Can the number of subsets of n nonnegative integer weights whose sum is at most a given capacity be estimated within 1±ε, with constant success probability, in Õ(n·poly(1/ε)) time? Feng and Jin’s randomized subquadratic counting algorithm leaves this natural input-linear target open.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The target uses the usual arithmetic/word-operation model, suppressing logarithmic dependence on encoded weights and capacity. An October 2026 deterministic improvement still does not attain this target: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14595
